title: Teach a claim a question can check
statement: Instruction must contain at least one concrete claim from which a check question with a definite answer and plausible wrong options can be written; otherwise no retrieval can follow it.
example: To pass, at least one question must be writable with a definite answer and at least 2 plausible wrong options.
detail: The video-script check fails a script so vague, hedged or opinion-based that no single unambiguous multiple-choice question can be derived from it (`shadow-bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/video_script/evaluation.txt`). To pass, at least one question must be writable with a definite correct answer and at least 2 plausible wrong options. The rubric justifies the check by the testing effect, citing Roediger & Butler 2011 by author and year only: retrieval right after instruction, it says, turns short-term exposure into durable memory.
against: Deliberately lenient: '**This is a low bar.**' (`shadow-bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/video_script/evaluation.txt`, line 433).

evidence.quote: The CFU is the primary encoding event — retrieval immediately after instruction is what converts short-term exposure to durable memory (testing effect; Roediger & Butler, 2011).
**Fail:** The script is so vague, so hedged, or so opinion-based that no single unambiguous MCQ can be derived from it.
- A definite correct answer (not "it depends" or "both could be right")
- At least 2 plausible but wrong distractors
